questions.q: Why might a privileged upbringing work against someone later in life?
a: Never having to struggle can leave them unprepared for real difficulty
Private schools teach fewer practical subjects than public ones
Wealthy parents rarely pass on any useful habits
Rich students are usually less intelligent than poor students
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that an easy life removes the challenges that build toughness.

questions.q: What does Gladwell say a learning disability can do?
a: Push people to over-develop strengths in other areas
Permanently limit achievement in every subject
Matter only for students in expensive schools
Disappear once a person reaches adulthood
questions.why: Lesson 2 says disadvantages can lead people to build compensating skills that more than make up for them.

questions.q: What did Princeton's harder-to-read test font show?
a: Reading more slowly helped students think and score better
Students gave up more often when text was unclear
Font style had no effect on test performance
Faster readers always produced the best answers
questions.why: Lesson 2 reports that average scores rose when the font forced slower, deeper thinking.

questions.q: How often do underdog armies win when they use guerrilla tactics?
a: About 63 percent of the time
About 29 percent of the time
About 10 percent of the time
About 90 percent of the time
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts a 63 percent win rate with guerrilla tactics against 29 percent without them.

questions.q: What let the British beat a larger fleet at Trafalgar?
a: Unconventional tactics that broke up the enemy formation
Ships that were larger and better armed than the enemy's
A sudden storm that destroyed most French vessels
Superior numbers gathered from nearby colonies
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the British attacking head-on and encircling parts of the fleet.
